findings.summary: The legend names the four line series but no null marker, so the solid triangle (solved magnetic axis), the hollow triangle (label magnetic axis), the solid cross (solved X-point) and the hollow cross (label X-point) appear in every one of the five panels with no key and no caption sentence saying which set is which. These panels exist to compare the solved state against the label state, and the axis comparison is exactly what the two triangles carry; a reader who cannot tell which is which reads the solved axis as the label's or the reverse. One extra legend entry per marker style, or one clause in the caption, closes it.

The five rendered panels are 1400x994, 1400x1088, 1400x991, 1400x992 and 1400x1003 px (aspect 1.287-1.413), so none sits on the declared 14x7.2 in slide canvas (1.94:1) and no two panels of one evidence set are the same size; saving with bbox_inches='tight' recomputes the canvas per panel instead of holding the declared one. The panels are still readable, but they cannot be dropped onto a slide at the declared size and they do not read as one set.

Frame 144's legend advertises 'Nova solved flux' and 'solved separatrix' with their swatches, but this panel draws neither: it carries only the grey label contours, the label axis and the wall. The caption does say the solve refused, so a reader is not left hunting for a blue line forever, but a legend that names two absent series sends them looking first. Suppressing the two solved entries when no solved field was drawn would make the key match the panel.

A red X-point marker is drawn to the left of the first-wall outline at roughly three-quarters vessel height, in white space outside the vessel, while a second X marker sits inside the lower vessel. A stationary point rendered outside the wall reads to a reader as a solved null in vacuum, which is either a genuine finding about the solve or an artefact of where the null was taken; the panel does not let a reader tell which, and no caption text addresses it.

A short blue solved-flux contour arc is visible at the bottom left of the vessel, below the first-wall polyline's bottom edge as that edge is drawn, while the panel's other contours stop at the wall. If it lies genuinely outside the vessel it is field the wall mask should have blanked, and it invites a reader to read solved flux outside the wall; if it is inside a divertor pocket, the drawn wall edge is what misleads. Worth a look at the panel before the next render.

The grey label level set shares the solved level array gauge-aligned, and in this frame the label field is compressed enough that its nine contours pack into a narrow bundle at the upper left, overlapping one another into a grey smear: a reader can see that the label field is displaced from the solved band, but cannot resolve the individual levels or the label field's shape. The compression is faithful to the data, so this records a limit on what the panel can show rather than a plotting error.
